global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred significance-oriented ordering, not a popularity list. The seven very recent papers each have zero current citations and zero influential citations in the Semantic Scholar lookup, so citation momentum cannot distinguish them.

sections.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
sections.abstract: For the stationary abelian sandpile on the square lattice, avalanches are almost surely finite, with the probability of reaching distance R bounded by a negative power of log R.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that adding a grain at the origin to the stationary sandpile on Z² almost surely stabilizes; the radius tail is at most C(log(R+2))^-a for constants C<∞ and a>0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The infinite-volume stationary state is the local limit of uniform recurrent sandpiles in wired finite boxes; the result concerns a single grain added at the origin.
sections.unique_caveat: The quantitative tail is only a negative power of log distance; the paper does not claim a sharp tail or finite expected avalanche radius.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Theorem 1.1 resolves a repeatedly posed question for the two-dimensional model and gives an explicit logarithmic-power tail bound; the proof links avalanche events to uniform spanning trees.

sections.title: Critical Ising model as the M(4,3) minimal model of conformal field theory
sections.abstract: The authors construct a correspondence from local spin polynomials in critical Ising to states of the M(4,3) minimal model and prove nontrivial scaling limits for all non-null fields on isoradial graphs.
sections.claimed_result: A surjective map sends each lattice spin polynomial to an M(4,3) state, with kernel exactly the null fields. For every non-null local field, suitable mesh rescaling yields a nontrivial scaling limit in correlations, expressed through minimal-model primary correlations and Virasoro action.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical Ising on isoradial graphs; the lattice mesh tends to zero, and observables are local polynomials in spins inserted in correlations.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns local spin-polynomial observables and the stated scaling-limit regime; it does not by itself classify every nonlocal observable or every boundary setup.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract and introduction claim a rigorous classification of all local spin-polynomial fields, not only selected primary observables; the paper bridges discrete complex analysis, probability, and conformal field theory.

sections.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
sections.abstract: Using canonical lifts, the author proves the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields and proves it for divisor classes in certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem A proves the integral geometric Tate conjecture for a Calabi-Yau threefold over a finite field if it is ordinary, or if it is strict and 1-ordinary. Theorem B treats divisor classes for 2-ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties with H²(X,O_X)=0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties over finite fields, under the stated ordinarity/strictness and cohomology hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem has ordinarity conditions; the broader-dimensional result is limited to divisor classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a concrete cycle-class-surjectivity theorem in algebraic geometry and number theory; canonical lifts transfer characteristic-zero results to positive characteristic.

sections.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture and reproduce the public Lean theorem declaration.
sections.claimed_result: The public Lean endpoint formalizes a prime connected-sum decomposition and, for each factor, torus cuts whose resulting interiors carry complete metrics locally modeled on Thurston geometries, with finite volume in the hyperbolic case.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Connected, closed, oriented smooth three-manifolds; the theorem returns prime factors and possibly noncanonical torus decompositions.
sections.unique_caveat: The formalized statement makes no uniqueness or canonical-JSJ-family claim for the cutting tori; the result is the precise encoded declaration and its verified Lean dependencies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a substantial proof-assistant artifact for a central three-manifold theorem; the paper exposes the endpoint declaration and explains its geometric interpretation and verification.

sections.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
sections.abstract: The authors construct a smooth negatively curved embedded annulus with convex boundary in tangent planes and two closed asymptotic curves, contradicting Nirenberg's 1962 conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: There exists a smooth embedded annulus in R³ with negative interior Gauss curvature, two distinct closed asymptotic curves, and strictly convex boundary components in parallel tangent planes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A smooth embedded annulus in Euclidean three-space with the specified curvature and boundary geometry.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction disproves the stated conjecture but does not settle all rigidity questions for negatively curved surfaces; the authors report checking computations in a Mathematica notebook, rather than a machine-checked formal proof.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a concrete counterexample to a named conjecture in differential geometry and connects it to rigidity of negatively curved surfaces.

sections.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
sections.abstract: The authors prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map for harmonic-map-flow solutions at finite-time singularities where only isolated bubbles form.
sections.claimed_result: A weighted Łojasiewicz–Simon inequality near a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling yields continuity of the body map in the isolated-bubble finite-time-singularity case.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Solutions of harmonic map flow with finite-time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated theorem is limited to isolated-bubble singularities; it does not claim the result for general bubbling configurations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a conjecture resolution, and the result is cross-listed between geometric analysis and PDE; its weighted Łojasiewicz–Simon inequality supplies an explicit analytic mechanism.

sections.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
sections.abstract: The authors establish sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products, including one-dimensional fibres, using comparison and spectral approximation methods.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds involving warped-product and boundary volumes, fibre Laplace eigenvalues, and base Steklov eigenvalues; comparison uses weighted Helmholtz–Steklov problems and spectral approximation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Warped products with compact Riemannian bases with boundary and closed Riemannian fibres; additional natural warping constraints are studied separately.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimates depend on geometric and spectral data of both base and fibre; the abstract does not imply a universal bound independent of those inputs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract says this supersedes earlier bounds, extends the setting to fibres of any dimension, and obtains sharp bounds; it is cross-listed in spectral theory, PDE, and geometry.
